about: The least lighting and general-use outlets of a dwelling's rooms, one rule set for each standard, read by `load_points` (loads.rs). Each row names its source, the standard's item; a test fails on one that does not. The numbers are the standard's, the words are ours. A country's set is added as a new entry, never as code. Room kinds: bath, kitchen (kitchen, pantry), service (service area, laundry), dry (living room, bedroom), veranda, other. `least` is the fewest outlets; `per_perimeter_m` asks one for each so many metres of perimeter, a whole number up, and only above `above_m2` when it is given; `counter` the outlets over a kitchen's sink counter; `first` points at `first_va` each and every other at `va`. The lighting is `va` up to `up_to_m2` and `step_va` more for each whole `step_m2` above. `alternative` lets `first` points be paid at `first_va` where the rooms that have `first` hold more than `above` points together.

rule_sets.source: ABNT NBR 5410:2004 (corrected version 2008), item 9.5.2, dwellings. Equivalents: IEC 60364 leaves the number of outlets of a dwelling to national rules; the US NEC, article 210.52, places receptacles by spacing along the walls instead; BS 7671 sets no count.

alternative.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.5.2.2.2 a), the alternative allowed where those rooms together have more than six points

rooms.source: NBR 5410:2004, 9.5.2.2.1 b) (count, two over the sink's counter) and 9.5.2.2.2 a) (power)
